title: Outlook for iPhone and iPad: refreshed interface in the Liquid Glass style
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap's default-on interface refresh and treats its elapsed target month as unconfirmed timing. The changed Outlook mobile release notes do not identify this Liquid Glass refresh, and fresh searches found no feature-specific switch, build requirement or separate charge that contradicts the briefing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Commercial users normally require an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 subscription including the Office desktop applications, subject to the stated small-screen exceptions.
claims.quote: However, commercial users require an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 subscription that includes the Office desktop applications:

claims.claim: Office 365 Enterprise E1 permits Outlook mobile on devices with integrated screens 10.1 inches diagonally or less.
claims.quote: Commercial users with the following subscriptions are allowed to use the Outlook mobile app on devices with integrated screens 10.1" diagonally or less: Office 365 Enterprise E1, Office 365 F1, Office 365 A1, Microsoft 365 Business Basic, and if you only have an Exchange Online license (without Office).
